Subject: AcmeData renewal: term extension & capacity increase

Thanks again for the chat this morning. AcmeData is ready to move forward with a 24-month renewal, but we need two updates before procurement can sign: a one-year term extension (from 12 -> 24 months in the order form) and a 35% capacity uplift across our standard ingestion and embeddings usage. Procurement asked us to get a clean order form and a marked MSA exhibit showing any SLA or term language changes.

Can you share the latest order form and a redline of Exhibit C (usage/coverage)? If legal can keep changes isolated to Exhibit C and the order form, procurement is comfortable avoiding a full MSA re-sign.

Attachments: — none from us yet.

Best,

I attached an initial clean order form (AcmeData_OrderForm_v3.pdf) with the 24-month term and a prorated billing schedule that lines up with your fiscal Qs. I've also attached a working draft of Exhibit C (MSA_Exhibit_C_DRAFT.docx) with the proposed capacity bands and the uplift reflected as an incremental tier.

- We attempted to limit substantive contract changes to Exhibit C and the order form; the MSA body is unchanged.

- SLA windows in Exhibit C are unchanged; instead, we added an explicit traffic-based burst policy to preserve latency SLOs during short spikes.

2) Karthik to confirm the technical mapping for the uplift (batching/region mapping).
3) I’ll prepare DocuSign once redlines are resolved.

Lauren / Karthik — quick first pass from Legal. I focused on keeping the core MSA untouched and limiting edits to Exhibit C as requested. High-level items:

1) Billing cadence: The order form proposes prorated billing aligned to your fiscal Q; we need a short clause confirming that proration applies only to the first invoice after signature (I added redline language to Exhibit C).
2) Capacity uplift: I preserved the tiered usage model but added a cap-trigger clause that protects Redwood from sustained overcommit (>150% of committed Q over a rolling 30-day window). That clause is soft — it requires notice and a remediation plan, not immediate termination.
3) Indemnity/insurance: No change to MSA body, but I called out that the uplift could increase maximum exposure for service-related claims; I suggested a dollar-band carveout in Exhibit C (see paragraph 4).
4) Data residency: Acme's earlier ask about EU residency wasn't in scope for this renewal; flagged for sales if this comes back.

I've attached a redline of Exhibit C (MSA_Exhibit_C_DRAFT.docx — redline track on). If we agree on the cap-trigger and proration language, we can keep this to Exhibit C and proceed straight to signature.

One ask for Sales: confirm whether Acme will accept the remediation-plan approach for sustained overages or whether procurement will insist on an immediate surcharge.

Marissa Cole
Senior Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MSA_Exhibit_C_DRAFT.docx (redline)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Solomon <maya@acmedata.com>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acmedata.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeData renewal: term extension & capacity increase

Thanks — looping in a short technical note so Procurement understands how the uplift maps to our capacity model.

- The 35% uplift has been modeled as a permanent shift to your committed baseline for Token Ingest and Embeddings. We recommend pinning that to region-us and region-eu split 80/20 to avoid cross-region throttling.
- For burst protection, the cap-trigger Marissa described is reasonable: if sustained usage exceeds 150% of the committed baseline over 30 days we'll notify and propose either (a) a temporary surcharge for the overage month, (b) a short-term reserved burst allocation, or (c) move to a higher committed tier.
- Implementation: no code changes required; we'll apply the tier change at the account level and confirm KV cache warming to avoid cold-start latency for heavier traffic.

Maya / Paul — does Procurement need technical language in Exhibit C or is the billing/contract language sufficient? If you want, I can add a one-paragraph technical mapping to Exhibit C that describes the region split and burst handling.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Solomon <maya@acmedata.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acmedata.com>, contracts@acmedata.com
Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 17:05:00 -0700

Lauren / Marissa / Karthik — thank you for the fast turnaround and clear redlines. Procurement reviewed and the team is comfortable with the approach, with two final asks before we sign:

1) Please swap the "cap-trigger" wording to explicitly state the remediation path will be our first option (notice -> remediation plan -> optional surcharge) rather than immediately defaulting to surcharges. Procurement wants the escalation path called out in the order form or Exhibit C.
2) Provide a short appendix (1 paragraph) in Exhibit C that maps the uplift to the region split Karthik suggested (80/20) so our cloud team has a record.

If you can incorporate those two items and resend a DocuSign-ready package by Monday EOD (PST), procurement will route for signature the same day.

Attachments referenced: AcmeData internal PO (PO-8892.pdf) — sent to contracts@acmedata.com separately.

Best,
